facts.subject: Business model
facts.statement: Atlas sells orchestration software subscriptions and separately priced implementation services.
facts.decision_impact: Defines whether recurring software economics can be separated from services.

facts.subject: ARR
facts.statement: Illustrative ending subscription ARR is 12.0 million currency units.
facts.definition: Contracted recurring subscription run-rate excluding implementation services
facts.decision_impact: Starting point for growth, retention, and valuation analysis.

facts.subject: Net revenue retention
facts.definition: Ending subscription ARR from opening cohort divided by opening subscription ARR
facts.decision_impact: Supports expansion but remains sensitive to cohort completeness.
facts.notes: Requires reconciliation to billing and general ledger records.

facts.subject: Delivery burden
facts.statement: Implementation services remain material and may constrain gross-margin scaling.
facts.definition: Analyst inference from disclosed delivery model
facts.decision_impact: Could reduce software-quality valuation and increase cash needs.
facts.notes: Needs project-level labor and gross-margin evidence.

claims.claim: The subscription base demonstrates early expansion within retained customers.
claims.decision_implication: Supports focused diligence but not final underwriting.
claims.next_test: Recalculate gross and net retention by cohort and reconcile to contracts, billing, and churn reasons.

open_items.question: Does reported NRR reconcile to customer contracts, billing, and churned accounts?
open_items.rationale: The preliminary thesis depends on expansion and low churn.
open_items.evidence_requested: Customer-level opening/ending ARR, contracts, invoices, cancellations, and cohort definitions
open_items.consequence_if_unresolved: Hold final IC and treat retention claim as provisional.
